requirement_text.REQ-063: Execute Decision 0006's D1 (docs/migration/decisions/0006-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md): relocate REQ-015's users, groups and tenant_role tables out of the public default schema and into each tenant's own Postgres schema, via the same :prefix mechanism and the same TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0 registry every business table already uses. This resolves the open question lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md section 7 has held open since REQ-022, and which identity-schema.md section 1 originally deferred. READ FIRST, IN FULL, BEFORE ANY CODE: decision 0006 (all of it, but section 3 especially), decision 0003 Dimension B plus its 2026-08-17 Addendum, and req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md sections 3.4/4/7. Section 4 of REQ-022's design is mandatory reading -- every migration this requirement writes MUST carry its prefix()-truthiness guard, or a plain mix ecto.migrate silently creates stray public-schema tables. THE SECURITY-SENSITIVE CORE is decision 0006 section 3: moving users per-schema changes the meaning of TWO shipped unique indexes. unique_index(:users, [:username]) becomes per-tenant rather than global (deliberate -- globally-unique usernames across tenants is a multi-tenancy defect, see 0006 section 3.1). The partial index users_external_identity_partial_index on (external_realm, external_id) likewise becomes per-tenant; 0006 section 3.2 argues the global one-OIDC-identity-per-user guarantee is RELOCATED to tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index rather than lost, because a realm binds to exactly one tenant immutably. That argument must be independently re-derived by SECURITY-REVIEWER, not accepted on this requirement's say-so. Also record in the users migration header the pre-existing divergence 0006 section 3.2 documents: 0003 line 132 and identity.ex:41 both describe the JIT upsert key as (tenant_id, external_realm, external_id) while the shipped index omits tenant_id -- this requirement closes that divergence rather than introducing a weakening. ORDERING IS NOT OPTIONAL (0006 section 4): register the three tables in tenant_scoped_migrations/0 with the section-4 guard; replay migrations across every registered tenant schema; copy each public row into the schema its tenant_id names (the last legitimate read of that column); drop the three public tables as a separate guarded step following GBL-112's precedent. Dropping tenant_id from users/groups is NOT this requirement -- it is REQ-064, and it must come after this one. tenant_role needs no constraint redesign: its own migration header (20260816000003) already anticipates this exact move and states its name index becomes unique-per-tenant-schema automatically. SCOPE BOUNDARY: this requirement does not touch AuthPipeline's step ordering -- 0006 section R5 verifies the existing realm -> tenant -> user order already resolves the tenant before any users query, so no pipeline rework is needed. It does not build 0006's D4 cross-tenant reporting mechanism. It does not drop any tenant_id column.

REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILed the first version of this design (see handoffs/WF02-REQ063-20260818/step-01b-design-gate.json) on check 2a -- a TBD/deferral. Your own §7 item 1 correctly identified that lib/letflow/identity.ex's public functions have no :prefix threading today and will break the moment your own §5 drop migration runs, correctly called this 'a hard precondition, not a nice-to-have' -- and then declined to design it, offering only an illustrative 'e.g.' instead of a committed signature change. That is the ONLY thing that failed. All five of your original design elements (the three migrations, the manifest entries, the data-copy mechanism including the tenant_role join-through-groups partitioning, the separate drop migration, and the explicit tenant_id-not-dropped scope statement) independently passed and do not need to change.

Fix required, scoped precisely so you don't over-expand: ORCH traced the actual blast radius before routing this rework, so you don't have to re-derive it from scratch. Of identity.ex's three public functions, only provision_oidc_user/3 touches the users table (via its private call chain: upsert_by_external_identity/3 -> get_by_external_identity/2 and insert_or_fetch/3 -> re_select_on_conflict/2 -> get_by_external_identity/2 again, three Repo calls total: Repo.insert at line 165, Repo.get at line 186, Repo.get_by at line 208, all in the private helpers below provision_oidc_user/3). resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 and verify_realm_ownership/2 both query Tenant, not User -- Tenant is a Decision-0006-D3 table that stays in the public schema, so those two functions need NO change. Design the concrete fix scoped to provision_oidc_user/3's call chain only: (a) the new @spec for provision_oidc_user/3 with an added prefix/tenant_schema parameter (or an opts keyword list carrying it -- your call, but commit to one), matching the existing lib/letflow/definitions.ex opts :: [prefix: String.t()] convention your own §7 item 1 already named as the pattern to follow -- read definitions.ex's actual usage of that convention (grep for 'prefix:' in lib/letflow/definitions.ex) before designing this, don't just cite it from memory; (b) the same threading through upsert_by_external_identity/3, insert_or_fetch/3, re_select_on_conflict/2, and get_by_external_identity/2's own signatures; (c) the exact call-site edit needed at lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex's provision_user/3 (private function, calls Identity.provision_oidc_user/3 at line 171) -- state what value it passes for the new parameter and how it obtains it (TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 on the already-resolved tenant.id, the same derivation REQ-043/execution's tenant_id-derivation contract already established elsewhere)stated concretely, not just 'AuthPipeline passes it'; (d) confirm whether this changes provision_oidc_user/3's error shape (a new {:error, :invalid_tenant_id}-shaped case if schema_name_for_tenant/1 fails) and state it explicitly per WF-02 Step 1's error-handling-shape requirement.

Once this is designed concretely, §5's drop migration's hard precondition is satisfied and you may state so plainly in §7 item 1's replacement text (either resolved-in-this-design, or, if you judge scoping it into THIS requirement is wrong, say so explicitly with a reasoned scope-boundary argument for ORCH to evaluate -- but 'flag and defer with no plan' is the one option already ruled out by the FAIL).

Produce lib/letflow/design/req063-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md covering every module this requirement touches, per WF-02 Step 1's procedure. This design executes decision 0006's D1 only (D2 -- dropping tenant_id -- is explicitly out of scope, reserved for REQ-064). Design-only: no implementation code, function signatures and @spec-style shapes only.

Specifically design: (1) three new tenant-scoped migrations (users, groups, tenant_role) following REQ-022 section 4's prefix()-truthiness guard pattern exactly -- state the exact table/index/constraint shape each carries, unchanged from the current public-schema migrations except for the prefix guard and, per decision 0006 section 3.2, closing the (tenant_id, external_realm, external_id) vs (external_realm, external_id) divergence in the users migration's index shape (state explicitly in the header comment that tenant_id's role in that key is now taken over by the schema boundary). (2) the three new entries appended to TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0's manifest, in the correct order relative to REQ-022/043's existing entries. (3) the data-copy mechanism (decision 0006 section 4 step 3): design the shape of a migration-time or one-off copy function that reads each public users/groups/tenant_role row and writes it into the tenant schema its tenant_id names via TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 -- state whether this is a mix task, a one-off script, or a migration itself, and its exact function signature. (4) the public-table-drop step (decision 0006 section 4 step 4), following GBL-112's guarded-separate-step precedent -- name the migration file and its guard condition. (5) state explicitly, per the requirement text, that dropping tenant_id from users/groups is OUT OF SCOPE for this design (reserved for REQ-064) -- the per-tenant copies of users/groups still carry tenant_id after this requirement ships.

Open questions to state explicitly, not silently resolve (decision 0006 section 7): whether tenants.status == :migrating gates the cutover, and how existing AuthPipeline/Identity tests that assume a public-schema users table need to change their setup (this may require test-fixture design guidance for TEST-DESIGNER, even though you don't write tests yourself).
